messages:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE on-call: KV hit-rate collapse observed for tenant MarlinFinance (vpc-prod-us-east-1) affecting generate/embedding endpoints. Severity: P1. See graphs: https://grafana.redwood/workspace/kv/marlin-2268

Alex Chen: I’m on it — acknowledge. Pulling query logs and hit-rate dash now.

Maya Patel: I can help with live mitigation. Do we know if this is a global KV issue or tenant-local?

Alex Chen: Initial read: high eviction rate on KV nodes in dedicated pool 12. Hit-rate for tenant namespace marlin/* fell from 92% -> 7% in ~3m. Other tenants in same pool still ~85%. So looks like tenant-local pollution.

Jamie Ortiz: Any recent deploys to Marlin or changes to their prefetch config? Customer eng tell me they rolled an A/B prefetch change at 08:05 UTC.

Oliver Brooks: Confirmed — Marlin changed prefetch window to 48h and turned off prefix hashing in their svc-config at 08:03. They rolled via our Private control plane.

Maya Patel: That aligns. Large prefetch set will warm a ton of prefixes and push out resident working set -> eviction storm.

Alex Chen: Impact: elevated 95th/99th token latency on marlin requests, some 504s from the model routing layer when KV misses spike. Customer reported increased tail latency.

Alex Chen: Live plan: 1) throttle Marlin prefetch traffic at edge 2) isolate their namespace from shared LRU admission (move to cold-only admission) 3) roll an emergency config revert on their prefetch service if they want rollback.

OpsBot: Executing command: /throttle tenant marlin rate=0.2 --scope=edge --reason=\"KV eviction storm\"

Alex Chen: Throttle applied at edge to 20% of prefetch requests. Monitoring...

Maya Patel: While throttle helps, eviction pressure persists because objects already resident. We should evict the largest prefetch prefixes first (prefixes starting with pfx:marlin/pf-*) to recover hit-rate for critical tokens. Can infra run targeted eviction?

Jamie Ortiz: I can do targeted eviction on pool 12. Will run an evict-list based on prefix regex. Confirm command?

Alex Chen: Use the safe-evict tool with dry-run first:
```
# dry-run to preview keys that would be evicted
./safe-evict --pool=12 --match=\"^pfx:marlin/pf-\" --dry-run --max-keys=5000
```
If output looks right, run without --dry-run.

Jamie Ortiz: Dry-run shows ~3.2k keys, mostly prefetch bundles. These are non-critical. OK to proceed in batches of 500.

Oliver Brooks: Notifying Marlin: we pushed a throttle and will evict bulk prefetch keys to restore service. Ask if they want a rollback of their prefetch flag.

Marlin Support (via customer channel): Thanks, appreciate it. We did a canary change, roll us back please — risk of churn.

Alex Chen: Understood, we’ll schedule rollback once immediate tail latency stabilizes. Proceeding with targeted evictions.

Jamie Ortiz: Running batch 1 evict (500 keys) on pool 12...

OpsBot: Evict job started (job_id=evict-226880-a1). ETA ~22s per batch.

Jamie Ortiz: Batch 1 complete. Observed hit-rate bump for marlin namespace from 7% -> 18%. 95th token latency down ~120ms.

Maya Patel: Good. Continue running batches until hit-rate >60% or until we’ve cleared the prefetch window.

Alex Chen: Also flipping their admission policy for marlin to cold-only to prevent re-priming during recovery:
```
# runtime API
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/marlin/runtime \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"admission_policy\":\"cold_only\"}'
```

OpsBot: runtime change applied: admission_policy=cold_only for tenant marlin.

Oliver Brooks: Noted. We should create a temporary circuit-breaker that rejects prefetch bundles > 256MB to prevent future overfill. Will propose config to Marlin.

Alex Chen: Agreed. Also create temp routing to divert new marlin traffic to warmback pool (pool 14) with clean cache to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Jamie Ortiz: Spawning migration job to route 25% traffic to pool 14 as canary.

OpsBot: Route-split applied: marlin -> pool12:75% pool14:25% (job_id=route-226880-b2).

Maya Patel: Monitoring shows pool12 hit-rate slowly recovering, pool14 has solid 88% hit-rate for marlin subset. Overall tail latencies trending down.

Alex Chen: Customer impact note for PS/Admin: Marlin observed intermittent 5–12% of requests with token-level latency spikes ~1.2–1.8s during peak of event. No data loss, only degraded latency and some TTL-based retries surfaced as 502s.

Oliver Brooks: For post-incident: we need a tenant-level guardrail: prefetch quotas, admission throttles, and a default prefix-size cap. Ops to propose and add to Private control plane policy.

Jamie Ortiz: Running remaining eviction batches (2..7) now. Batch 4 shows hit-rate at 55%.

Alex Chen: When we hit >60% steady for 10m, we can consider re-enabling admission. Also schedule a rollback of their prefetch change since Marlin asked.

Marlin Support: Rollback please. Their canary caused unexpected amplification.

Alex Chen: Initiating rollback request via control plane (cc: CustEng Oliver).

OpsBot: Rollback request submitted to tenant control plane (req_id=rb-226880).

Jamie Ortiz: Evictions complete. Hit-rate now 72%. 95th token latency back within SLO for marlin. No new 5xxs in the last 8m.

Maya Patel: Flipping admission_policy back to normal but keep prefetch throttle until their config is reverted.

Alex Chen: Re-enable admission to default:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/marlin/runtime \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"admission_policy\":\"default\"}'
```

OpsBot: admission_policy restored. Prefetch throttle remains at 20% until rollback completes.

Oliver Brooks: Customer rollback completed on their end per CustEng. Removing throttle and lifting route-split will be next after 15m stable.

OpsBot: Removing throttle... done. Route-split reverting to pool12:100%... done.

Alex Chen: Monitoring stable. Final hit-rate steady at 85%. Marking incident mitigated. Will start a brief postmortem and action items:
- enforce prefetch quotas in control plane
- add targeted eviction tooling to safely prune oversized prefetch bundles
- tenant-level alert for sudden prefetch/eviction deltas
- update runbook to include route-splitting pattern used here

Maya Patel: On-call handoff to Maya for follow-up and postmortem draft.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Closing page. :white_check_mark:

OpsBot: Incident marked mitigated (incident=INC-226880)
